newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices fall in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices fall in late trade.

text.p: Profit-taking eroded Taiwan stocks' earlier gain in late Tuesday trade, as brokers said they had detected no signs of government-orchestrated buying to mark the first anniversary of President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration.
With 65 minutes to go, or 0255 GMT, the weighted index fell 51.25 points or 0.63 percent at 8,056.29.
Turnover was a weak T$35 billion.

"Hopes that the government will engineer a celebration rally are fading. There is no sign the government has intervened to boost share prices so far," said Lin Long-hsien, an analyst of United Securities.
"On the other hand, we cannot rule out the possibility that the state-related buying will emerge later," Lin added.
Minor buying interest concenstrated on previous laggards, rubber shares, which rose 1.15 percent.
